claims.text: Equiatomic NbZrTiHfMo is a disordered BCC solid solution in the as-cast state.
As-cast equiatomic NbZrTiHfMo has a room-temperature compressive yield strength of 1719 MPa.
Equiatomic NbZrTiHfMo has limited room-temperature plasticity.
The limited plasticity of equiatomic NbZrTiHfMo is primarily caused by Mo-induced embrittlement.
A controlled heat-annealing treatment can create nanoscale structural heterogeneity in equiatomic NbZrTiHfMo.
Annealing at 650–750°C for 2–6 hours followed by quenching will promote coherent nanoscale precipitates or nanotwins.
The induced coherent precipitates or nanotwins will be fine and uniformly dispersed within the disordered BCC matrix.
The nanoscale precipitates or twins will delay crack initiation.
The nanoscale precipitates or twins will act as barriers to crack propagation.
The nanoscale precipitates or twins will provide additional sites for dislocation generation and motion.
Enhanced dislocation generation and motion will promote distributed plastic deformation and strain hardening.
The proposed mechanism will mitigate Mo-associated embrittlement without significantly reducing intrinsic yield strength.
After treatment, compressive yield strength will remain within approximately 5–10% of 1719 MPa.
After treatment, room-temperature compressive plastic strain will increase markedly relative to the untreated alloy.
The beneficial effect is limited to annealing conditions that produce nanoscale features.
Excessive annealing temperature or duration may cause precipitate coarsening or phase separation.
Precipitate coarsening or phase separation would degrade strength and negate the ductility improvement.

contradictions.description: The target is repeatedly described as as-cast, but the conditions specify homogenization before annealing. Homogenization changes the starting state, so it is unclear whether the tested baseline is truly as-cast or homogenized.
